summary: Fresh comprehensive testing of TruthScan MVP - all critical flows verified. Backend: 16/16 tests pass. Frontend: All major features working including text/URL analysis, chatbot, dashboard, guest mode.

minor.issue: Test assertion in previous test file used old label names ('Fake', 'Likely Misleading') — fixed to match actual labels ('Likely False', 'Misleading / Missing Context', etc.)

integration_issues.issue: Review request mentions /analyzer but actual route is /analyze (no 'r'). Guest users going to /analyzer get redirected to home. This is a navigation note, not a code bug.

issues: Wikipedia page (misinformation topic) returns 'Misleading / Missing Context' (37/100) — the NLP heuristics flag Wikipedia's CAPITALIZATION-heavy text and references to flat earth, COVID etc. as suspicious. Not a bug but expected NLP limitation.

critical_code_review_comments: Route is /analyze not /analyzer — documentation/review request had typo. No code change needed.
Wikipedia URL analysis returns low credibility score due to NLP heuristics detecting CAPITALIZATION in article. Acceptable for NLP-based system without real LLM.
seed_data_creation: 1 text analysis and 1 URL analysis created for test user during testing
context_for_next_testing_agent: All core flows verified: Auth (login/logout/signup/guest), text analysis (correct labels: Likely False/True/etc), URL analysis (works, ~12s for Wikipedia), chatbot (floating panel opens after analysis, responds to 'Why this verdict?' with reasoning+phrases), dashboard (charts + history table). Route is /analyze (not /analyzer). Capabilities endpoint returns ocr:true, url_extraction:true, web_search:true. Image tab UI renders but OCR not tested end-to-end (no image file available in test env).
